messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT INC-2026-172: Hosted API queue growth detected — GPU autoscaler failing to provision. p95 generation latency up 4x, p99s spiking; backlog increasing. Autoscaler error sample: `provisioner: allocate failed: quota_exceeded`  

nate: Seeing large fanout from a partner campaign — overall RPS up ~6x in last 10m. Hosted request queue length jumped from ~1k to ~18k. p95 ~2.1s -> 8.7s, p99 ~12s -> 42s, timeouts increasing. Customers hitting 30s timeouts. :eyes:

sre-jen: Paging oncall. I'm taking primary. Assigning ops-harper as infra support. Harp, can you check provisioner leader and GPU pool state?

ops-harper: On it. Quick checks: `kubectl -n provisioner get pods` shows leader pod CrashLoopBackOff on provisioner-0. Logs show repeated AWS quota errors and 429 from cloud provider. Paste of tail:```
ERROR provisioner/allocator.go:241 allocate: failed to create instance: RequestLimitExceeded: Request throttled
  status code: 429, request id: xyz-abc
```

product-kim: Heads-up — two enterprise customers reported degraded completions via support. Kim will coordinate comms.

support-luis: I've opened tickets for the two impacted accounts and set SLO incident template. Both report high latency and some 502s when requests hit our gateway timeout.

sre-jen: Mitigation plan (executing now):
1) Enable fallback routing to `gpt-medium-quant` (lower-cost variant) for non-SLA traffic.
2) Apply temporary global token-throttle policy for anonymous projects: 10 rps per org.
3) Pause non-critical batch jobs hitting hosted to free up queue capacity.
4) Manual scale-up attempt of dedicated GPU pool while we debug autoscaler leader.

nate: I just flipped fallback routing for routes tagged `nonprod` and `low-priority` — logs show immediate drop in queue length for those routes.

ops-harper: Manual scale-up attempted but cloud provider is returning quota errors on new instance creations. Trying fallback region and different instance family. Running:```
aws ec2 request -region us-west-2 --instance-type p4d --count 2
```
Response: `Client.RequestLimitExceeded` — throttled.

sre-jen: If cloud provisioning is throttled, let's enable soft-fallback to CPU-backed quantized model for a subset of high-volume non-latency-sensitive traffic. Nate and I will update routing rules. Also increasing autoscale retry backoff to avoid hammering provider.

deploy-bot: :robot_face: Rollout started: route-change-fallbacks v2 -> canary (5%). Logs available: https://console.internal/redwood/rollouts/2387

nate: Canary looks good for low-priority traffic. Queue for host:api-low dropped ~35% in 3m. High-priority tenants still stuck.

product-kim: Drafting customer notice. Key points: degraded latencies, mitigations applied, ETA unknown pending cloud quota clearing. Will share draft in #general-internal for approval.

support-luis: Adding an interim workaround for customers: suggest switching to `model=fast-small` or retry with exponential backoff for now. Including that in tickets.

ops-harper: Provisioner leader log shows heartbeat loop saturated; restarting provisioner leader pod now. If that doesn't free the queue we may need to drain a few non-critical pools.

sre-jen: Restart complete. Provisioner came back but still slow; provider continues to reply 429. Preparing escalation to cloud account team for quota bump and rate limit reset. Opening cloud-support case now (case #CS-7891).

infra-bot: Incident update: backlog peaked at ~21.3k requests at 1739999930; currently 9.1k after fallbacks and throttles. 

nate: Observability note — KV cache hit rate unchanged; this is pure capacity shortage not caching behavior.

ops-harper: We managed to provision 2 smaller GPU instances in fallback region (eu-west-1) and started routing 12% of high-priority traffic there. Latency for that shard p95 improved from 38s -> 6.2s.

product-kim: External comms approved: short notice + mitigation steps + guidance for enterprise customers to turn on region pinning to avoid impacted region. Sent to affected contacts.

support-luis: Two customers already confirmed improvements after switching to pinned eu-west-1 region. Recording for postmortem.

sre-jen: Next steps:
- Keep throttles and fallbacks until cloud quota cleared and autoscaler stable.
- Track customer-impacted list and SLA exposures.
- Postmortem owner: nate (timeline + root cause).
- Action: add autoscaler backoff and provider-429 detection to alerting.

nate: I'll own the postmortem. Early RCA: sudden partner-led RPS blast + provider-side request throttling + insufficient autoscaler backoff led to provisioner leader instability and delayed recovery.

ops-harper: Filed runbook update PR with extra diagnostic commands and a retry policy tweak: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/provisioner#pr-412

sre-jen: Closing oncall handoff in 30m. If we see new quota errors after cloud support responds, escalate to eng-runtime. Otherwise we'll keep the safeguards for 12-24h.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-172 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Recorded metrics: peak backlog 21.3k, peak p99 42s, affected enterprise customers: 2 open tickets.

product-kim: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups tomorrow and include mitigation timeline in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

support-luis: Logging final notes in ticket system. Marking tickets as 'investigating -> mitigated' for now.

nate: Postmortem will include timeline, partner traffic source, autoscaler tuning recommendations, and an action to add provider-429 automatic fallback routing. Expect draft within 48h.

sre-jen: Thanks team — good mitigations. Handoff complete.
